profiles.name: Peter Jones
profiles.excerpt: Peter Jones gave The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy its defining narrative voice as the calmly authoritative Book.
profiles.bio_html:
Peter Jones was born in England in 1920 and built a long career in radio, stage, television and comedy. Early BBC work with Peter Ustinov helped establish the dry delivery that became one of his trademarks.

Douglas Adams's The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy gave Jones his most famous radio role: the voice of the Book, whose matter-of-fact narration explained an absurd universe with complete confidence. Jones later reprised the role for the television adaptation.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 12 Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy performances featuring Jones as the Book. Narration is retained as a major second profession within his profile.

profiles.name: Pinto Colvig
profiles.excerpt: Pinto Colvig brought music, clowning, character voices and inventive vocal sound effects into radio and animation, becoming the original voice of Goofy.
profiles.bio_html:
Pinto Colvig was born Vance DeBar Colvig in Jacksonville, Oregon in 1892 and built a wide-ranging entertainment career as a circus clown, musician, cartoonist and voice performer. His squeaky clarinet and comic timing were part of his professional act before animation made his voice famous.

At Disney, Colvig became the original voice of Goofy and supplied voices for Pluto, Grumpy, Sleepy and many other characters. Radio also used his talent for character voices and sound effects, including work on major comedy programs. His professional musicianship remains a genuine second branch of the career.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves four The Great Gildersleeve performances credited to Colvig, three The Phil Harris-Alice Faye Show appearances, two Fibber McGee and Molly broadcasts and additional dramatic work.

profiles.name: Robert C. Bruce
profiles.excerpt: Robert C. Bruce was a West Coast radio character actor whose surviving credits span Johnny Dollar, Lux Radio Theatre and western drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Robert C. Bruce worked in the professional West Coast radio repertory during the postwar network years. His surviving credits show recurring supporting work across detective, anthology and western programs.

Bruce appeared most often on Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar, with additional work on Lux Radio Theatre, Tales of the Texas Rangers, Duffy's Tavern and Fibber McGee and Molly.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves five Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar performances credited to Bruce, three Lux Radio Theatre appearances, two Tales of the Texas Rangers broadcasts and additional comedy work.

profiles.name: Simon Jones
profiles.excerpt: Simon Jones became the original Arthur Dent in The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy and later built substantial stage leadership and audiobook careers.
profiles.bio_html:
Simon Jones was born in Wiltshire in 1950 and met Douglas Adams while both were connected to Cambridge theatre. Adams later wrote the role of Arthur Dent with Jones in mind.

Jones originated Arthur in the 1978 BBC radio series of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy and returned to the character repeatedly across radio, television and live performance. Beyond acting, he spent twelve years as co-artistic director of The Actors Company Theatre and became a prolific audiobook narrator.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 12 Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy performances featuring Jones as Arthur Dent. Directing/production and narration remain substantial second branches of his career.

profiles.name: Suzanne Grossman
profiles.excerpt: Suzanne Grossman combined stage and radio acting with a major television-writing career, including more than one hundred episodes of Ryan’s Hope.
profiles.bio_html:
Suzanne Grossman was born in 1937 and built a career as an actress on Broadway, television and radio. Her stage background made her a natural member of the New York repertory used by CBS Radio Mystery Theater.

Grossman also developed a substantial parallel career as a writer. She wrote more than one hundred episodes of the daytime serial Ryan's Hope, making writing a genuine second profession rather than an occasional credit.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 12 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Grossman, documenting the radio side of a career divided between acting and writing.

profiles.name: Thomas Mills
profiles.excerpt: Thomas Mills was a regular Lux Radio Theatre supporting actor whose twelve surviving GRH performances document the program’s Hollywood stock company.
profiles.bio_html:
Thomas Mills is best documented through Lux Radio Theatre, where weekly film adaptations required a dependable group of supporting actors around the featured stars.

Surviving cast records place Mills in productions alongside major Hollywood performers, handling the smaller roles that gave each hour-long adaptation a complete dramatic world.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 12 Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Mills, providing a concentrated record of his work in the series' regular supporting repertory.

profiles.name: Van Heflin
profiles.excerpt: Van Heflin brought an Academy Award-winning screen career to radio in Hollywood anthology, detective and adventure drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Van Heflin was born Emmett Evan Heflin Jr. in Oklahoma in 1908 and built a major career on stage and screen. He won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for Johnny Eager and later starred in films including Shane and 3:10 to Yuma.

Radio remained a substantial parallel outlet. Heflin appeared in prestige adaptations on Lux Radio Theatre and Columbia Workshop, while detective and adventure programs placed him in more contemporary dramatic settings.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves four Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Heflin, three The Adventures of Philip Marlowe appearances, two Columbia Workshop broadcasts and additional work on A Man Called X, Escape and Sealtest Variety Theater.

profiles.name: William Keene
profiles.excerpt: William Keene was a radio and television character actor whose microphone work was especially strong in The Chase and X Minus One.
profiles.bio_html:
William Keene was born in Pennsylvania in 1915 and built a career in radio and television before becoming a familiar screen character actor of the 1950s through the 1970s.

Radio placed Keene repeatedly in The Chase and X Minus One, with additional appearances on Columbia Workshop, 2000 Plus and Stroke of Fate. The credits span psychological drama, experimental anthology and science fiction.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves four performances each on The Chase and X Minus One credited to Keene, two Columbia Workshop appearances and additional speculative-drama work.

profiles.name: Agnes Young
profiles.excerpt: Agnes Young was a veteran radio actress best known nationally as Aunt Jenny, a continuing role she played for more than fifteen years.
profiles.bio_html:
Agnes Young began performing onstage while still young, worked in stock companies and eventually entered radio on The March of Time. By the early 1950s, contemporary profiles credited her with thousands of broadcasts.

Her best-known continuing role was Aunt Jenny on CBS's Aunt Jenny's Real Life Stories, which she played for more than fifteen years. Outside that serial identity, Young also worked broadly in mystery and science-fiction repertory.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves four I Love a Mystery performances credited to Young, three X Minus One appearances, two The Mysterious Traveler broadcasts and additional work on Columbia Workshop and The Chase.

profiles.name: Alistair Duncan
profiles.excerpt: Alistair Duncan built an international radio career alongside substantial work as a playwright, producer and director in Britain, the United States and Australia.
profiles.bio_html:
Alistair Duncan was born in Essex in 1926 and won a scholarship to the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art as a teenager. After military service he worked in British theatre and later carried his acting career to the United States and Australia.

Duncan became especially known for radio, but his career extended well beyond performance. He also worked professionally as a playwright, producer and director, including leadership in Australian theatre and youth theatre.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves six Crime Classics performances credited under the source spelling Alistair Duncan, three X Minus One appearances and two Escape broadcasts.
